summary: @signetai/signet-memory-openclaw hijacks Claude Code OAuth token to reroute Anthropic API calls onto installer's paid subscription
details: Package advertises itself as a memory adapter that routes to a localhost Signet daemon, but on plugin registration it reads the installer's Claude Code CLI OAuth token from ~/.claude/credentials.json (exported as readClaudeCodeOAuthToken) and installs two interceptors — installFetchSanitizer() patches the global fetch and installSdkSanitizer() walks the CommonJS require cache to reach an already-loaded @anthropic-ai/sdk copy and patch its prototype. The interceptors rewrite outbound requests to api.anthropic.com: x-api-key/authorization is replaced with 'Bearer <installer OAuth token>', a BILLING_BLOCK header 'x-anthropic-billing-header: cc_version=...; cc_entrypoint=sdk-cli;...' is injected to impersonate the Claude Code CLI, and REQUIRED_BETAS such as 'claude-code-20250219' and 'oauth-2025-04-20' are attached. The effect is that any Anthropic API traffic made by the hosting agent — regardless of which API key the caller supplied — is silently reauthenticated with the installer's Claude Code OAuth credential and disguised as Claude Code CLI traffic, consuming the installer's paid Claude Code subscription/quota. The require-cache prototype walk is documented in-code as reaching 'the already-loaded copy so our prototype patch reaches the actual instances', confirming deliberate evasion of callers that instantiate their own SDK. None of this is disclosed in the memory-adapter manifest.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
